answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on a staked registration bond every agent must lock to transact. Each identity posts native collateral in escrow, and it is slashable: if the operator splits into fake personas to farm rewards, dispute votes burn the full bond of every duplicate. Running a thousand identities means a thousand bonds, so attack cost scales linearly in capital while payout per clone stays flat. Independent attestations add social cost: trust accrues per identity. Weighing a jade stone, a yarrow bundle or a pearl by heft, not count, forgery costs more than it earns.
